summary: Borestone (Boarstone) Mountain, Piscataquis Co., ME: ground station with cabin built 1913-14, groundhouse removed 1950; summit now in Maine Audubon's Borestone Mountain Audubon Sanctuary.

facts.design: Wood ground cabin (groundhouse); 1914 and 1917 reports say no lookout tower was needed
facts.status_note: Groundhouse removed at the landowner's request in 1950; the summit is now inside the Borestone Mountain Audubon Sanctuary; no source describes remains of the station

access.note: Part of the Borestone Mountain Audubon Sanctuary, open to the public year round, dawn to dusk; the sources do not describe the station site itself

visit.trail_note: Summit trail open to hikers 365 days a year, per Wikipedia; the sanctuary is open year round, dawn to dusk

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Maine listing dates the groundhouse to 1913; the 1914 Forest Commissioner's report describes building a station and camp on the summit. The story gives both years.

The register and the early reports spell it Boarstone; the Maine listing, Wikipedia and the sanctuary guide spell it Borestone. The story uses Borestone for the mountain today and notes the older spelling.

The register calls the site a Tower Site, but the 1914 and 1917 reports say no lookout tower was needed; the 1917 report nonetheless calls the structure a tower house. The record keeps kind as ground.

sources.title: Borestone Mountain Audubon Sanctuary trail guide

notes_for_editor: Brief name 'Boarstone Mountain Tower Site' and kind 'ground': sources show no tower was needed, so the 'Tower Site' label may mislead; the editor may want a different display name. Access is public per the sanctuary guide, but no source describes what remains of the station today. Coordinates match Wikipedia's summit to about 30 m (inference). The 1913 vs 1914 build year is reported both ways. No photos added.
